title: Genitive 5: есть vs нет
description: After есть the noun stays in the nominative. After нет it shifts into the genitive. Drill the alternation.
descriptionRussian: После есть существительное остаётся в именительном падеже. После нет переходит в родительный.
intro: This is the lesson where the case becomes visible. Take one sentence, change a single word in it, and watch the noun at the end change shape in response. Nothing else at A1 shows you so plainly what a case actually is: not a property of a word, but a reaction to something else in the sentence. If cases have felt abstract until now, that stops here. Read each pair twice.
rules: After есть, the noun stays in the nominative (its dictionary form). У Маши есть книга. У Антона есть кот.
After нет, the noun shifts into the genitive. У Маши нет книги. У Антона нет кота.
The same noun changes form depending on the trigger: есть keeps it; нет shifts it. Always check the trigger word in the prompt before choosing the form.
examples: У меня есть книга. (I have a book.) Nominative.
У меня нет книги. (I don't have a book.) Genitive.
У Антона есть машина. (Anton has a car.) Nominative.
У Антона нет машины. (Anton doesn't have a car.) Genitive.
У нас есть молоко. (We have milk.) Nominative.
У нас нет молока. (We don't have milk.) Genitive.

items.promptEnglish: There is no phone in the office.
items.explanation: Recap from previous lessons: нет triggers genitive. Телефон is masculine consonant: + -а → телефона. Today's lesson adds the contrast with есть, which keeps the nominative.

items.hint: After есть, the noun stays in which case?
items.explanation: After есть the noun stays in the nominative, with no case shift. Сестра is the dictionary form. Compare with 'У Маши нет сестры,' where нет triggers genitive (-а → -ы).

items.hint: Нет triggers genitive. What does feminine -а become here?
items.explanation: Книга is feminine -а. Нет triggers genitive: -а → -ы, and the spelling rule writes -и instead of -ы after к, г, х, ш, ж, щ, ч. So книги.

items.hint: Есть or нет: which one keeps the nominative?
items.explanation: Есть keeps the nominative. Брат stays as the dictionary form. The есть/нет alternation is the cleanest way to feel the case shift: брат (есть) ↔ брата (нет).
Нет triggers genitive. Окно is neuter -о: swap to -а → окна. The pattern works the same regardless of the subject (у нас, у меня, у Антона, etc.).

items.hint: After есть the noun stays in...?
items.explanation: Across all three genders, есть keeps the noun in the nominative. Яблоко (neuter) is no exception. The flip side: 'У Лены нет яблока' would have the genitive form.

blanks: У Антона нет _____. (Anton doesn't have a son.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Сын is masculine consonant. Нет triggers genitive: + -а → сына.

errorCorrection.sentence: У меня есть машины в гараже на даче.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I have a car in the garage at the dacha.
errorCorrection.explanation: After есть the noun stays in the NOMINATIVE: машина. The form машины is the genitive, and that's exactly the form you'd use after нет ('у меня нет машины', 'I don't have a car'). The pattern is есть → nom, нет → gen, a clean reversal.

errorCorrection.sentence: У нас нет молоко в холодильнике сегодня утром.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: We don't have any milk in the fridge this morning.
errorCorrection.explanation: After нет the noun shifts into the genitive: молока. Молоко is the nominative (used after есть: 'у нас есть молоко'); after нет it must take the gen ending: neuter -о → -а gives молока.

errorCorrection.sentence: У Маши есть друга в этом городе уже несколько лет.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha has had a friend in this city for several years now.
errorCorrection.explanation: After есть the noun stays in the NOMINATIVE: друг. The form друга is genitive, and that's the form Lesson 1 introduced for the нет construction ('у Маши нет друга'). The same noun, two opposite cases depending on есть vs нет. Russian is consistent: presence → nom, absence → gen.

minimalPairs.explanation: After есть the noun stays in the nominative: сестра. The genitive form сестры appears in the opposite construction: 'У меня нет сестры' (I don't have a sister).
After нет the noun shifts into the genitive. Яблоко is neuter -о, so the genitive is яблока. Contrast with 'У Маши есть яблоко,' where яблоко stays in the nominative.

reviewVocab.definition: there is / one has (after есть, the noun stays in the nominative)
nominative case (the dictionary form, used after есть)
reviewVocab.example: После есть существительное стоит в именительном падеже: 'У меня есть телефон.'

reviewVocab.definition: genitive case (used after нет, for absence and possession)
reviewVocab.example: После нет существительное стоит в родительном падеже: 'У меня нет телефона.'
